title: Effective fppf descent of finite-type algebraic spaces
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], over schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T$ be a scheme, let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], and let $X_i\to T_i$ be algebraic spaces of finite type: they are quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose given isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TX_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$, with $\varphi_{ii}$ the identity on the diagonal and $\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ after pullback to each triple overlap. There exists an algebraic space $X\to T$ and isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\cong X_i$ inducing precisely the given $\varphi_{ij}$. Fibre products mean sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No countability assumption on $I$ is required.

proof.text: Regard each $X_i$ as a sheaf on the big fppf site of $T_i$, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The maps $\varphi_{ij}$ are isomorphisms of these restricted sheaves and satisfy the sheaf descent cocycle. Use the small skeleton in [def-weil-size-convention] to apply [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the given covering. This constructs a sheaf $F$ on the big fppf site of $T$ and isomorphisms $e_i:F|_{T_i}\simeq X_i$ satisfying $e_j=\varphi_{ij}e_i$ on each double overlap. In particular $F\times_T h_{T_i}\simeq X_i$ as sheaves over $T_i$. Algebraicity of $F$ is the remaining issue.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal B(T)$ for the set of affine open subschemes of $T$. Refine the schemes $T_i$ by affine open subschemes. Restricting a flat locally finitely presented map to an open subscheme preserves both properties by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The images of these affine pieces in $T$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and cover $T$. For each affine basis open $B\subset T$ that is contained in at least one such image, choose one affine piece $V_B\subset T_{a(B)}$ whose image contains $B$. The selected images still cover: for any $t\in T$, first take an image containing $t$, then an affine open $B$ with $t\in B$ contained in it. Each $V_B$ is affine and $V_B\to T$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; so [lem-sfb-bounded-affine-lft-coproduct], applied to the one-member family, makes $V_B$ isomorphic over $T$ to an object of the big fppf site, and we replace $V_B$ by that object. Let $J$ be the set of basis opens for which a choice was made. Thus $|J|\leq|\mathcal B(T)|$, and $\{V_j\to T\}_{j\in J}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. If $T$ is empty, choose $J=\varnothing$. This argument uses affine opens rather than a bound on the cardinality of the point set of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: For $j\in J$ put $P_j=F\times_T h_{V_j}$. The isomorphism $e_{a(j)}$ identifies it with $X_{a(j)}\times_{T_{a(j)}}V_j$. This is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and its map to $V_j$ is of finite type by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus]. As $V_j$ is affine, quasi-compactness of this finite-type morphism says exactly that $|P_j|$ is quasi-compact. This uses quasi-compactness over an affine test scheme, without imposing quasi-separatedness on $P_j$.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $W_j\to P_j$ with $W_j$ affine by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The map $W_j\to V_j$ is locally of finite type: it is an etale scheme-chart test of the locally finite type map $P_j\to V_j$, with the chart meaning stated in [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus]. The map $V_j\to T$ is locally finitely presented and hence locally of finite type; composition preserves local finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Consequently $W_j\to T$ is locally of finite type. No finiteness assertion about the etale atlas as a morphism is used.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] form $E=\coprod_jW_j$. Step 2 gives $|J|\leq|\mathcal B(T)|\leq\max\{\aleph_0,|\mathcal B(T)|\}$, and step 4 gives affine schemes $W_j$ locally of finite type over $T$. Thus [lem-sfb-bounded-affine-lft-coproduct] gives a representative of $E$ in the original big site over $T$. Explicitly, if $\theta:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E_0$ is the isomorphism over $T$, use $\theta\circ\iota_j:W_j\to E_0$ as the coproduct maps: any family of maps from the $W_j$ extends uniquely by precomposing its extension from $E$ with $\theta^{-1}$. Thus $E_0$ is itself a scheme coproduct in the fixed site. Applying [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct] to the atlases $W_j\to P_j$ now gives an algebraic space $P=\coprod_jP_j$ in fppf sheaves. Its required atlas-source size hypothesis has therefore been verified in the fixed site, including when $J$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: Similarly let $D=\coprod_jV_j$, with its map $p:D\to T$. The $V_j$ are affine, and $V_j\to T$ is locally of finite type by the local-finite-presentation implication in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By [lem-sfb-bounded-affine-lft-coproduct] choose an isomorphism $\delta:D\xrightarrow{\sim}D_0$ over $T$ with $D_0$ in the original big site. Its structure map is $p_0=p\circ\delta^{-1}$ and its component maps are $\delta\circ\iota_j$; hence $p_0\circ\delta\circ\iota_j=p\circ\iota_j$ for every $j$. Replace $D,p$ by $D_0,p_0$: the coproduct universal property follows by composing extensions with $\delta^{-1}$, as in step 5. Its component inclusions are disjoint open immersions covering $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Flatness and local finite presentation of $p$ follow on these components by source locality in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; its surjectivity follows from the jointly surjective family in step 2. Hence $p$ is a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme morphism.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: The maps $P_j\to F$ induce $q:P\to F$. To identify its scheme tests, fix a scheme $Z$ and a section $a\in F(Z)$. By [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition], a section of $h_Z\times_F P$ over any test scheme $Z'\to Z$ consists of a clopen partition $Z'=\coprod_jZ'_j$ and sections of $P_j$ over $Z'_j$ mapping to $a|_{Z'_j}$. Since $P_j=F\times_T h_{V_j}$, those sections are exactly maps $Z'_j\to V_j$ over $T$; the $F$-component is already fixed. By the scheme coproduct universal property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], these data are exactly a map $Z'\to D$ over $T$, obtained by gluing on the indicated disjoint open cover. Conversely a map to $D$ gives this partition by inverse images of the coproduct components. These inverse constructions commute with restriction, so $h_Z\times_F P\simeq h_{Z\times_T D}$. The constructions keep the $Z$-section fixed, so the projection to $Z$ is the usual scheme base change of $p$. In particular the structural map $P\to T$ is the composite $P\to F\to T$, since this equality holds on every coproduct summand.

proof.text: The scheme-test projection in step 7 is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by base-change stability in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to the morphism $p$ of step 6. In particular $q:P\to F$ is representable by schemes, hence by algebraic spaces, and satisfies exactly the scheme-test hypotheses of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap]. Here $F$ is the sheaf constructed in step 1 and $P$ is the algebraic space constructed in step 5. The bootstrap theorem proves that $F$ is an algebraic space over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0ADV, lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2), scheme-base case; expanded using Tag 04U0, lemma-locally-algebraic-space-finite-type. The affine-basis refinement below repairs the insufficient point-indexed size estimate.

proof.text: Take $X$ to be this algebraic space with underlying sheaf $F$. The isomorphisms $e_i$ from step 1 give $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$. Their comparisons are precisely $\varphi_{ij}$, because the descent construction imposed $e_j=\varphi_{ij}e_i$ before any refinement. Morphisms of algebraic spaces are morphisms of their sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], so these are the required algebraic-space isomorphisms. The proof used a bounded refinement of the original covering only to establish algebraicity; it imposed no countability restriction on $I$.
